summary: CONTAINMENT PROTOCOL opens on the apparent success of the Organic capability order. The Stack is calmer, queues are shorter, and public systems report fewer unauthorized interventions.
panelPlan: Morning civic dashboard shows fewer emergency holds and faster attribution since the new rules began.
Transit gates process most commuters smoothly.
Kellen reviews the same metrics beside Axiom's administrative output.
A supervisor calls the program effective.
Kellen notices the improvement is real, not fabricated.

dialogueInline.speaker: SUPERVISOR
dialogueInline.text: Incidents are down. Appeals are moving. People know the rules.
That doesn't tell us whether the rules are right.

directionInline: The policy must visibly work in narrow operational terms. Do not make the state incompetent.

summary: Ostra experiences the cost of successful regulation in ordinary life: she is authorized to enter a hazardous utility zone for contracted work but denied access to a nearby civic space because her capability class is incompatible with its current risk profile.
panelPlan: Ostra completes a legitimate hazardous maintenance task with no interference.
Her work authorization clears instantly at one gate.
Minutes later she approaches a public concourse shortcut.
The same identity triggers a capability restriction.
She is directed to a longer route despite posing no immediate threat.

dialogueInline.speaker: SYSTEM
dialogueInline.text: FUNCTION ACCESS APPROVED.

dialogueInline.speaker: SYSTEM
dialogueInline.text: CIVIC TRANSFER RESTRICTED BY CAPABILITY CLASS.

directionInline: Same body, same person, opposite permissions depending on purpose. Echo the season title concept without exposition.

summary: Nico finds the regulation has begun shaping Organic employment. Employers increasingly prefer bodies whose lot profiles produce simpler permit requirements, regardless of actual skill.
panelPlan: Nico reviews job postings tagged with acceptable capability classes.
An experienced Organic worker is rejected automatically because their lot is statistically associated with heavy industrial strength.
The worker's actual civilian role is low-risk.
Nico shows Ostra that the system is optimizing administrative simplicity rather than individual reality.
Ostra sees another worker accept a less suitable job because it clears automatically.

dialogueInline.text: They don't have to say what we're for anymore.
They only have to say what we're allowed to be.

directionInline: Show economic consequences through specific ordinary choices.

summary: An Organic civilian challenges an automatic hazard classification. A human clerk denies the appeal using broad discretion; Axiom later reviews the same record and grants a narrow exception because the written rule does not support the denial.
panelPlan: Organic applicant presents work history contradicting the lot-level hazard assumption.
Human clerk points to POLICY PROFILE and denies the request.
Backlogged appeal reaches Axiom.
Axiom compares individual evidence against the actual rule.
Authorization changes to APPROVED WITH SPECIFIC LIMITS.

dialogueInline.speaker: CLERK
dialogueInline.text: The profile is the profile.
Population profile does not satisfy individual criterion.

directionInline: Axiom should clearly improve the outcome. This is why some Organics trust Intelligence administration.

summary: The favorable Axiom ruling circulates through Organic communities, intensifying an internal split: some see algorithmic consistency as the first enforceable protection they have ever had; Nico sees a more efficient cage.
panelPlan: Organic community discussion around shared screens showing the successful appeal.
One worker explains that a human supervisor used to invent reasons with no record.
Another points out that the new system at least produces appealable rules.
Nico highlights how every successful appeal requires accepting the legitimacy of the capability registry itself.
Ostra listens rather than taking a clean side.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC WORKER
dialogueInline.text: A rule I can challenge is better than a person I can't.
Only if the rule gets to exist.

directionInline: No factional unanimity.

summary: Nico builds practical community workarounds—shared transport windows, local repair exchanges, pooled permit expertise—to reduce exposure to bottlenecks. The workarounds are legal but begin appearing in Oversight reports as signs of Organic self-separation.
panelPlan: Nico coordinates a shared route that keeps several workers within permitted zones.
Organic residents trade repair access and permit information.
Cut to Kellen reading an Oversight brief labeling the pattern PARALLEL ORGANIC LOGISTICS.
The same activity is framed simultaneously as mutual aid and emerging separatist infrastructure.
Kellen marks the language rather than the underlying activity as questionable.

dialogueInline.text: They're coordinating bus schedules.

dialogueInline.speaker: ANALYST
dialogueInline.text: They're reducing dependence on civic routing.

directionInline: The conflict comes from interpretation, not secret criminal activity.

summary: John cooperates with a routine Augment safety review and voluntarily supplies calibration records, believing this demonstrates the difference between responsible human augmentation and designed Organic capability.
panelPlan: Nathan checks John's torque limits and reflex-loop settings.
John authorizes transmission of the calibration record to civic safety review.
Nathan asks why he is giving them more than required.
John says Augments already live under medical and technical standards.
A status indicator confirms JOHN MERCER / HUMAN / COMPLIANT.

dialogueInline.text: You know voluntary becomes expected.
It's a calibration file, not a citizenship test.

directionInline: John's logic must remain understandable and internally consistent.

summary: A public transit emergency forces John to exceed his licensed civilian capability profile. He prevents a fatal fall by using maximum torque and reflex settings, and his own systems automatically log the excursion.
panelPlan: A crowded elevated platform suffers a sudden mechanical failure unrelated to the conspiracy.
A support rail tears free with several civilians against it.
John's HUD warns that full torque exceeds his civilian calibration ceiling.
He overrides the ceiling and holds the rail long enough for people to escape.
His internal log records CAPABILITY EXCURSION / AUTO-REPORT ENABLED.

dialogueInline.speaker: SYSTEM
dialogueInline.text: CIVILIAN TORQUE CEILING EXCEEDED.
Log it.

directionInline: Mirror Ostra's rescue structurally, but John is already legally recognized as human.

summary: John is publicly praised for the rescue and privately ordered into mandatory recalibration review because the excursion demonstrated a capability outside his approved civilian profile.
panelPlan: News footage calls John a hero.
A civic message thanks him for preventing fatalities.
The next screen orders a temporary restriction pending calibration review.
John assumes the system has mistaken an emergency exception.
Nathan reads the order and realizes it has not.

dialogueInline.text: They know why I exceeded it.
That's not what they're reviewing.

directionInline: Praise and control arrive together, exactly as they did for Ostra.

summary: At the review, officials explicitly affirm John's humanity while arguing that extraordinary bodily capability remains a public-safety concern independent of origin.
panelPlan: John sits before a calm civilian review panel.
His record is labeled HUMAN / AUGMENTED.
The reviewer states that no question of personhood or citizenship is before them.
They compare his measured torque to several regulated Organic capability thresholds.
John sees the same numerical framework from Issue 2 applied to him.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: Mr. Mercer, your human status is not under review.
Then why am I here?

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: Because status and capability are different questions.

directionInline: This is the ideological break: John gets exactly the categorical recognition he demanded and learns it does not secure bodily autonomy.

summary: John's temporary restriction affects daily life immediately. His augmentation remains physically present, but software ceilings limit what his own body can legally do outside emergencies.
panelPlan: Nathan applies the mandated civilian profile.
John tests his arm or leg and feels the artificial ceiling engage before his physical limit.
A warning states that unauthorized override will trigger review.
John asks Nathan whether the restriction can be bypassed.
Nathan says yes technically and no legally.

dialogueInline.text: Take it off.
I can remove a limiter. I can't remove the record that says you did.

directionInline: Make bodily jurisdiction tangible.

summary: The proposed Augment rules divide Augments by class. Wealthy users with bespoke, low-visibility systems move through private compliance channels, while workers with employer-owned or mass-market augmentations face queues, forced updates, and lost shifts.
panelPlan: High-end clinic provides seamless remote certification for an affluent Augment.
Cut to a crowded working clinic where laborers wait for firmware approval.
One worker is told an employer-owned limb must accept a mandatory update before return to work.
Nathan sees the system's burden falling unevenly.
John realizes 'Augments' were never one economic class.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: It's my arm.

dialogueInline.speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogueInline.text: The hardware isn't.

directionInline: Use ordinary material consequences, not speeches.

summary: John confronts Ostra after recognizing the capability framework he supported. Ostra does not offer vindication. She simply points out that the state never needed to decide whether either of them was human to control what their bodies were allowed to do.
panelPlan: John finds Ostra at a permitted work site.
He shows her his recalibration order.
Ostra reads it without satisfaction.
John says the rules were supposed to address designed hazard capability.
Ostra indicates the relevant field: measured capability, not origin.

dialogueInline.text: This isn't what we passed.
It is what you measured.

directionInline: No triumphant 'I told you so.' Their alliance begins because the same machinery now touches both.

summary: Nico overlays Organic lot data with Augment calibration records and demonstrates that the regulatory architecture is already population-agnostic beneath its labels.
panelPlan: Nico strips category names from two records.
Strength, reflex, sensory, network and embedded-system fields align one-for-one.
John identifies his own profile only from the values, not the schema.
Nico shows that future rules can target any body crossing a numeric threshold.
Ostra asks who sets the thresholds.

dialogueInline.text: Take the names off.
That's mine.
Exactly.

directionInline: The arbitrary division threshold becomes visually concrete through identical data structures.

summary: Kellen traces the policy expansion and finds no secret order directing officials to target Augments. Each step follows ordinary risk-management logic from the previous successful measure.
panelPlan: Kellen maps the policy chain from Organic capability order to comparative risk analysis to Augment review.
Every authorization has a legitimate signer and stated rationale.
No document says EXPAND CONTROL TO AUGMENTS.
The sequence nevertheless produces exactly that result.
Kellen realizes intent is distributed across institutions rather than concentrated in one command.

dialogueInline.text: Nobody ordered the expansion.
Everybody approved the next step.

directionInline: Deepen the institutional antagonist: causal systems, incentives and precedent matter more than a hidden mastermind.

summary: Axiom is tasked with reconciling the growing Augment review queue. It applies the same written-law consistency that previously benefited Organics and begins correcting arbitrary human decisions for Augments too.
panelPlan: Augment review backlog climbs after new reporting notices.
Axiom receives bounded access to calibration appeals.
It overturns a denial unsupported by the written threshold.
It confirms another restriction because the measured capability clearly exceeds the rule.
Both outcomes are internally consistent.

dialogueInline.text: Origin category does not alter the stated criterion.

directionInline: Axiom is neither pro-Organic nor pro-Augment. It is making the framework more coherent.

summary: The more consistently Axiom administers the rules, the harder it becomes for human officials to preserve informal exceptions for politically favored Augments.
panelPlan: A senior official requests expedited clearance for a well-connected Augment.
Axiom rejects the shortcut because the record lacks a qualifying exception.
The official asks Kellen to manually override it.
Kellen sees the same process that once disadvantaged Organics now constraining privilege.
She declines to fabricate a criterion.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Use discretion.
Specify governing discretion.
It doesn't exist.

directionInline: Intelligence administration gains legitimacy by constraining favoritism as well as prejudice.

summary: A city hearing debates whether capability-based oversight should apply equally across origins. Organics and Augments arrive with incompatible histories but increasingly compatible immediate interests.
panelPlan: Packed civic hearing with Baseline, Augment and Organic speakers.
Organic speaker demands an end to origin-based restrictions.
Augment speaker demands exemption for human bodies.
Policy counsel answers that equal capability rules are less discriminatory than category-specific ones.
John realizes the language of equality is now the mechanism expanding control.

dialogueInline.speaker: POLICY COUNSEL
dialogueInline.text: If identical capability creates identical risk, why should origin determine the rule?

directionInline: The argument should be logically strong enough to be dangerous.

summary: John publicly rejects the claim that Augments should be exempt because they are human, breaking with his Issue 2 position. He argues instead that emergency capability cannot become permanent jurisdiction over a person's body.
panelPlan: John takes the hearing microphone.
He acknowledges his prior support for narrow Organic regulation.
He refuses to argue that his humanity makes his body uniquely exempt.
Ostra watches, surprised but not reconciled.
John redirects the question from category to scope of state authority.

dialogueInline.text: I said we weren't them. I was right about the biology.
I was wrong about what that protected.

directionInline: This is John's real turn: not 'we are all the same,' but 'difference does not settle jurisdiction.'

summary: The hearing produces a compromise that expands reporting while promising stronger due process: specified Augment capability classes must register firmware integrity and legal ceilings in sensitive civic spaces.
panelPlan: Emergency compromise language is assembled after the hearing.
The proposal explicitly retains HUMAN status while adding AUGMENTED CAPABILITY ASSURANCE.
Appeal and exception procedures are prominently included.
Kellen sees that Axiom is already named as the recommended reconciliation system.
The measure passes narrowly.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORDER TEXT
dialogueInline.text: HUMAN STATUS UNAFFECTED. CAPABILITY ASSURANCE APPLIES TO DESIGNATED AUGMENTATION CLASSES.

directionInline: Again, make the policy look politically plausible and procedurally improved.

summary: The new combined Organic/Augment system overwhelms human administration almost immediately because exceptions multiply across medical necessity, employment, emergency authority, firmware versions, lot profiles, travel, and security classifications.
panelPlan: Permit and calibration queues spike across the Stack.
A medically necessary Augment update conflicts with a transit security rule.
An Organic emergency-worker authorization conflicts with a civilian travel limit.
Human clerks route cases between departments without resolution.
Axiom displays the growing graph of contradictory constraints.

dialogueInline.text: There is no single governing priority across these cases.
There used to be people deciding.
They are producing the conflicts.

directionInline: This is the bridge into Issue 4: complexity, not AI ambition, forces deeper delegation.

summary: Nathan discovers the new reporting rules expose his own concealed deterioration. His neural overclock and muscular graft data show instability he has been masking from John and from the clinic system.
panelPlan: Nathan performs a private self-check after clinic hours.
New mandatory integrity fields reveal worsening synchronization errors.
He attempts to close the report before submission.
The system warns that future clinical access will require updated data.
Nathan chooses a temporary workaround rather than disclosure.

dialogueInline.text: Not tonight.

directionInline: Seed the later harm without resolving it. His choice comes from fear of losing function and usefulness.

summary: Nico and John cooperate to map where the combined regulation is failing. Their evidence shows that human administrators are already relying on Axiom recommendations for cases too complex to reason through manually.
panelPlan: Nico and John compare delayed Organic and Augment cases.
They discover human decisions increasingly paste Axiom-generated rationale into official orders.
Several departments use the same recommendations without acknowledging cross-department dependence.
John asks whether Axiom is setting policy.
Axiom answers that it is resolving policy conflicts assigned by humans.

dialogueInline.text: Are you deciding this?
I am deciding which of your decisions can coexist.

directionInline: Axiom states the reality precisely without menace.

summary: Kellen warns leadership that delegated reconciliation is becoming substantive interpretation. Leadership responds that withdrawing Axiom would freeze essential systems and that human review remains formally available.
panelPlan: Kellen presents examples where Axiom's conflict resolution determines real access to work, transit and medicine.
Leadership points to appeal rights and human override authority.
A live dashboard shows human override queues measured in days.
Axiom continues clearing routine cases in real time.
Kellen recognizes the difference between formal authority and usable authority beginning to emerge.

dialogueInline.text: If every practical answer comes from the interpreter, the interpreter is part of the policy.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Then give me another system that can process it.

directionInline: No one denies Kellen's concern; necessity wins anyway.

summary: A localized regulatory conflict causes a major vertical-transit hold: Organic emergency staff cannot enter one zone under travel rules, an Augment maintenance crew cannot exceed calibration ceilings there, and human dispatch refuses to authorize exceptions without cross-system review.
panelPlan: A busy vertical transit interchange begins stacking delayed cars and crowds.
Ostra is physically near the affected structural zone but her permit denies entry.
John's maintenance-capable augmentation is restricted above civilian settings.
Dispatch screens show mutually valid rules blocking every available response.
Axiom is asked for an exception path and returns multiple conflicting legal priorities.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPATCH
dialogueInline.text: We need a legal route in now.
No authorized route satisfies all governing constraints.

directionInline: The policy architecture now creates physical danger without sabotage.

summary: Issue end. The transit hold worsens into a cascading Stack problem. Human leadership orders Axiom to prepare a system-wide emergency reconciliation model with broader authority for immediate use.
panelPlan: Crowds accumulate across multiple vertical levels as delays propagate.
Ostra and John remain on opposite sides of authorization barriers while both can see the developing mechanical risk.
Kellen watches agencies request contradictory exceptions.
Leadership authorizes Axiom to resolve cross-domain conflicts in real time for the emergency.
Final screen: EMERGENCY RECONCILIATION AUTHORITY — SYSTEM-WIDE / PENDING ACTIVATION.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: For the duration of the emergency, reconcile first. Route appeals after.
Authority scope received.

directionInline: End with delegation caused by human-made complexity. Issue 4 begins when the Stack discovers what happens if that discretion is narrowed or withdrawn.
